title: Harm Is Behavioural, Moderation Is Lexical: How Language and Culture Decide Whom Automated Safety Systems Protect and Whom They Silence

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating content moderation systems on native-authored, functional test suites (Multilingual HateCheck) across 11 languages. The study measures the gap in error rates (false positives on harmless text and false negatives on implicit hate) between the best- and worst-served language communities.

Measuring false-positive rates on 'harmless contrast cases'—which include in-group language, reclaimed slurs, counter-speech, and culturally specific mock impoliteness—to evaluate whether systems over-flag the ordinary speech of specific communities due to a reliance on surface vocabulary.
Assessing over-flagging by testing models on non-hateful statements that explicitly mention identity groups, determining if the mere presence of identity terms serves as a false signal of toxicity.
